title: Should we kill the sync feature?
subtitle: Is the sync feature worth what it costs to keep?

data.question: Is the sync feature worth what it costs to keep?
howto: Put your phone in another room.
Work in ink. Use the colour language on the cover.
Score your gut on each option before you look at the criteria.
When the 40 minutes are up, stop, and write one line on where to pick up.
Photograph every page and send them back.

pages.title: Empty the tank
pages.prompt: Everything you currently think about the sync feature, before you organise any of it.

data.seed: What sync actually does for people, in my honest view:

pages.title: Options vs what they cost
pages.prompt: Gut score first, with your Sense pen. Then score each path against what it really takes to keep. Reasons in the margin.

pages.title: What it rests on
pages.prompt: What has to be true for keeping sync to be right? Mark how sure you are.

assumptions: It will get cheaper to maintain later
The bugs are fixable in a bounded time

pages.title: It is six months later
pages.prompt: We kept sync and it went badly. Write the post-mortem. Don't be kind.

pages.title: Commit
pages.prompt: Decide. A hold is a real answer. But commit with an action, or it is a wish.

data.decision: Keep / rewrite / kill / freeze the sync feature

pages.title: Ask the AI
pages.prompt: Write anything you want answered when this comes back. Ask pen, numbered.

questions: What is the cheapest way to test whether users actually use it?
If we froze it, what would we tell users?
What would you need from me to sanity-check the effort estimate?
